paragraph: This cluster of dermatological images consistently presents skin lesions with notable **color variegation**, encompassing a spectrum from light tan and medium brown to very dark brown and black within the same lesion, indicating a non-uniform pigment distribution. A key morphological characteristic shared across all images is the **pronounced asymmetry** in both their overall shape and internal structure. The **borders are consistently irregular and ill-defined**, often appearing notched, fuzzy, or showing evidence of pigment extending outwards into the surrounding skin. This manifests either as prominent radial streaks or pseudopods emanating from a darker central core (as seen in images 2 & 3), or as irregular, confluent projections and irregular scalloping (as in images 1 & 4). Morphologically, the lesions display **irregular contours**, varying from broadly irregular shapes to distinctly stellate or spiky forms. The internal patterns are heterogeneous, lacking uniform texture or structure, and instead showing a mix of granular areas, structureless dark patches, or a disordered radial arrangement. The common visual elements thus include multiple shades of brown/black, a clear absence of symmetry, and poorly demarcated, spreading or spiculated edges. These distinctive features—specifically the combination of marked asymmetry, significant color diversity, and highly irregular, often effaced or radially streaked borders—make this cluster recognizable as lesions exhibiting atypical and disorganized growth patterns.
